summary: Build practical digital finance controls for fraud, AML, CDD, and resilience. Explore case-based training and request a tailored course plan.
lede: Operational risk and compliance for digital financial services training helps you identify, assess, control, monitor, and report risks across mobile money, digital lending, agency banking, card payments, and related operations. It addresses fraud, transaction monitoring, customer due diligence, outsourcing, complaints, agent activity, and accountability across financial institutions and fintechs. You will build risk and control matrices, calculate key risk indicators, map fraud scenarios, configure sample monitoring rules, and prepare a supervisory evidence pack. Practical work with Excel-based analysis, dashboards, investigations, and control documentation is supported by structured coverage of AI-assisted monitoring, model governance, and regulatory trend analysis.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make, test, supervise, or report decisions about digital financial services risk and compliance. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with regulated financial products and need a structured, operational approach to fraud, AML, operational resilience, and customer protection.
prerequisites: Prior experience in banking, microfinance, payments, mobile money, digital lending, compliance, fraud, operations, or financial supervision is recommended. You should have working exposure to risk registers, customer onboarding, transaction processing, or regulatory control reviews. No programming is required. Exercises use operational application of Excel and dashboard concepts, while AI-assisted monitoring and model governance remain at conceptual awareness level.
